title: Marie Curie: The Woman Who Changed Science

sentences.en: In 1867, in the city of Warsaw, Poland, a girl named Maria Sklodowska was born.
sentences.zh: 1867年，在波兰华沙，一个名叫玛丽亚·斯克沃多夫斯卡的女孩出生了。

sentences.en: She would grow up to become Marie Curie, one of the greatest scientists in history.
sentences.zh: 她后来成为玛丽·居里，历史上最伟大的科学家之一。

sentences.en: Maria loved school more than anything else in the world.
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚热爱上学，胜过世上一切。

sentences.en: But in those days, Poland was ruled by foreign powers, and women were not permitted to attend university there.
sentences.zh: 但在那个年代，波兰被列强统治，女性不被允许上大学。

sentences.en: So Maria made a secret plan with her older sister Bronya.
sentences.zh: 于是玛丽亚和姐姐布罗妮亚定下了一个秘密计划。

sentences.en: Maria would work for years to pay for Bronya's education in Paris.
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚先打工多年，供布罗妮亚去巴黎读书。

sentences.en: Then, in return, Bronya would help Maria to study.
sentences.zh: 之后布罗妮亚再反过来帮助玛丽亚求学。

sentences.en: For six years, Maria worked as a governess in the countryside.
sentences.zh: 整整六年，玛丽亚在乡下当家庭教师。

sentences.en: She taught rich children during the day.
sentences.zh: 她白天教富人家的孩子。

sentences.en: At night, alone in her cold room, she studied chemistry and mathematics by candlelight.
sentences.zh: 夜里，她独自在寒冷的房间里就着烛光自学化学和数学。

sentences.en: In 1891, at the age of twenty-four, Maria finally boarded a train for Paris.
sentences.zh: 1891年，二十四岁的玛丽亚终于登上了开往巴黎的火车。

sentences.en: There she became a student at the Sorbonne, one of the most famous universities in the world.
sentences.zh: 在那里，她成为世界名校索邦大学的学生。

sentences.en: Life in Paris was harder than she had expected.
sentences.zh: 巴黎的生活比她预想的更艰难。

sentences.en: She lived in a tiny room on the top floor of an old building.
sentences.zh: 她住在老楼顶层的一个小房间里。

sentences.en: In winter, she was so cold that she wore every coat she owned to bed.
sentences.zh: 冬天冷得她只能把所有的外套都穿上睡觉。

sentences.en: Some nights, she ate only a piece of bread and drank weak tea.
sentences.zh: 有些晚上，她只吃一片面包、喝一点淡茶。

sentences.en: But she never complained, because knowledge was worth any price to her.
sentences.zh: 但她从不抱怨，因为对她来说，知识值得付出任何代价。

sentences.en: She graduated at the top of her class in physics.
sentences.zh: 她以物理专业第一名的成绩毕业。

sentences.en: In Paris, she met a young scientist named Pierre Curie.
sentences.zh: 在巴黎，她遇到了年轻科学家皮埃尔·居里。

sentences.en: They discovered that they shared the same dream, and in 1895 they married.
sentences.zh: 他们发现彼此怀有同样的梦想，并于1895年结婚。

sentences.en: Together, they worked in a small, broken laboratory with a leaking roof.
sentences.zh: 他们一起在一间屋顶漏雨、破旧狭小的实验室里工作。

sentences.en: Marie chose to study the strange rays that came from a metal called uranium.
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚选择研究一种名叫铀的金属发出的神秘射线。

sentences.en: These rays were invisible, but they carried surprising power.
sentences.zh: 这些射线看不见，却带着惊人的能量。

sentences.en: Other scientists had reported them, but nobody could explain them.
sentences.zh: 别的科学家曾报告过它们，但没有人能解释它们。

sentences.en: Marie's careful experiments produced clear evidence that something entirely new was hiding inside the rock.
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚细致的实验提供了清晰的证据：岩石里藏着某种全新的东西。

sentences.en: In 1898, she discovered not one new element but two.
sentences.zh: 1898年，她发现的新元素不是一种，而是两种。

sentences.en: She named the first one polonium, after her home country, Poland.
sentences.zh: 她把第一种以祖国波兰命名为"钋"。

sentences.en: The second one, which glowed faintly in the dark, she called radium.
sentences.zh: 第二种元素在黑暗中发出微光，她称之为"镭"。

sentences.en: The work of obtaining pure radium was almost impossible.
sentences.zh: 提取纯镭的工作近乎不可能完成。

sentences.en: To obtain even a tiny spoonful, she and Pierre had to boil tons of dark rock in huge pots, year after year.
sentences.zh: 为了提取哪怕一小勺，她和皮埃尔年复一年地用大锅熬煮成吨的黑色矿石。

sentences.en: The laboratory had no protection of any kind, because nobody yet knew the rays were dangerous.
sentences.zh: 实验室里没有任何防护，因为当时还没有人知道那些射线是有害的。

sentences.en: In 1903, Marie, Pierre, and the scientist Henri Becquerel shared the Nobel Prize in Physics.
sentences.zh: 1903年，玛丽亚、皮埃尔与科学家亨利·贝克勒尔共同获得诺贝尔物理学奖。

sentences.en: It was the first Nobel Prize ever given to a woman.
sentences.zh: 那是史上第一次有女性获得诺贝尔奖。

sentences.en: Only three years later, in 1906, Pierre was killed in a street accident.
sentences.zh: 仅仅三年后的1906年，皮埃尔在一场街头事故中丧生。

sentences.en: The sadness nearly destroyed Marie, but she refused to stop working.
sentences.zh: 悲痛几乎击垮了玛丽亚，但她拒绝停止工作。

sentences.en: She took over Pierre's position and became the first female professor at the Sorbonne.
sentences.zh: 她接过了皮埃尔的职位，成为索邦大学第一位女教授。

sentences.en: In 1911, she won a second Nobel Prize, this time in chemistry.
sentences.zh: 1911年，她第二次获得诺贝尔奖，这次是化学奖。

sentences.en: She was the first person in history to win two Nobel Prizes.
sentences.zh: 她是历史上第一位两次获得诺贝尔奖的人。

sentences.en: During the First World War, Marie saw that army doctors needed a way to look inside the bodies of injured soldiers.
sentences.zh: 第一次世界大战期间，玛丽亚看到军医们需要一种查看伤员身体内部的办法。

sentences.en: So she invented small, portable X-ray machines that could travel to the front lines.
sentences.zh: 于是她发明了可以运往前线的小型便携式X光机。

sentences.en: The soldiers called these little machines "petites Curies" — little Curies.
sentences.zh: 士兵们称这些小机器为"小居里"。

sentences.en: She trained her teenage daughter Irene and about a hundred and fifty other women to operate them.
sentences.zh: 她训练自己十几岁的女儿伊蕾娜和大约一百五十名女性学会操作。

sentences.en: Over a million soldiers were examined with these machines before the war ended.
sentences.zh: 战争结束前，超过一百万名士兵借助这些机器接受了检查。

sentences.en: Marie never protected herself from the rays she loved.
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚从未防护过她所热爱的那些射线。

sentences.en: After years of radiation, her health was slowly destroyed.
sentences.zh: 多年的辐射慢慢摧毁了她的健康。

sentences.en: She died in 1934, from a blood disease caused by her own work.
sentences.zh: 1934年，她死于由自己的工作引发的血液疾病。

sentences.en: Even today, her notebooks are kept in lead boxes in a Paris library.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，她的笔记本仍存放在巴黎一家图书馆的铅盒里。

sentences.en: They are still radioactive, so scientists who wish to read them must sign a promise to protect themselves.
sentences.zh: 它们仍带有放射性，想查阅的科学家必须签署防护承诺书。

sentences.en: Marie Curie's life teaches a simple lesson.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·居里的一生教给我们一个朴素的道理。

sentences.en: Real courage is not shouting loudly; it is the ability to endure hardship quietly and keep working.
sentences.zh: 真正的勇气不是高声呐喊，而是默默忍受困苦、坚持工作的能力。

sentences.en: She once said, "Nothing in life is to be feared; it is only to be understood."
sentences.zh: 她曾说："生活中没有什么可畏惧的，它只需要被理解。"

sentences.en: Because of her, science learned to see the invisible, and girls everywhere learned to dream bigger.
sentences.zh: 因为她，科学学会了看见不可见之物，世界各地的女孩也学会了做更大的梦。

questions.q: Why couldn't Maria attend university in Poland?
options: She failed the entrance exams.
Women were not permitted to attend university there at that time.
Her family forbade her to study.
Warsaw had no universities at all.
questions.explain: "women were not permitted to attend university there" —— 当时的波兰不允许女性上大学。

questions.q: How did Maria help her sister Bronya first?
options: She worked as a governess for six years to pay for Bronya's education in Paris.
She lent her radium samples.
She taught her chemistry at home.
She wrote her university essays for her.
questions.explain: 姐妹间的秘密计划：玛丽亚先打工六年供姐姐读书，姐姐再回报她。

questions.q: Why did Marie name the first element she discovered "polonium"?
options: Because it glowed in the dark.
After her home country, Poland.
After her husband, Pierre.
After her sister, Bronya.
questions.explain: "She named the first one polonium, after her home country, Poland" —— 以祖国波兰命名。

questions.q: Why are Marie Curie's notebooks kept in lead boxes today?
options: They are extremely old and valuable.
They are still radioactive from her experiments.
They contain secret military formulas.
The library is too small for shelves.
questions.explain: 笔记至今仍有放射性，查阅者须签署防护承诺 —— 这是她一生工作的代价。

questions.q: According to the passage, what is real courage?
options: Shouting loudly when facing problems.
Enduring hardship quietly and continuing to work.
Winning two Nobel Prizes.
Refusing to sleep or eat.
questions.explain: 结尾点题："the ability to endure hardship quietly and keep working"。
